text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Mubarak says he held positive and honest talks with Clinton and U.S. administration officials. President discusses with Congress leaders ways to achieve just peace and to boost joint cooperation.
- Suzanne Mubarak says in Paris that her Unesco award is in honour of Egyptian women's efforts.
- Grand Mufti says al-Azhar's Islamic Research Academy allows organ transplants.
- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Ebeid to take immediate steps to end losses of textile factories and to repay their bank loans.
- Agriculture banks to cut fertiliser prices to help farmers; two million tonnes of fertiliser to be made available to farmers who grow wheat, rice and summer products.
- Two seven-year-old children swallow rat poison because of humiliation at school and at home; one dies, the other is saved at the last minute.
- Agriculture minister says Egypt will cultivate 1.83 feddans of rice this season.
